text:
For a pellet smoker, a power station of about 1 kWh with an inverter rated at least 600 W is the right size. I'd skip the 300 W units.

**Why that size**
- A pellet grill draws little once it's lit. The auger, fan and controller use roughly 35–60 W. Only the igniter spikes, to about 200–500 W for a few minutes, according to [Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill) and [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight).
- Volt & Valley says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook, about 16 hours at 50 W. Dealectric reports one measured run of a Z Grills smoker on a Jackery Explorer 1000 that used 210 Wh in 6 hours.
- [BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker) estimates a higher average draw of 150–250 W. If your grill runs that high, a 1 kWh unit gives roughly 3–5 hours instead of overnight. Plug in a watt meter and check before you rely on it.
- A 300 W inverter with a 600 W surge is marginal against a 350–500 W igniter ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)). That rules out small units like the EcoFlow RIVER 3.

**Options from the results**
- **ALLPOWERS P1800 (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W):** This is the best value I found, at $399 on pre-order and shipping Dec 7 ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)). It has the capacity for an overnight cook and plenty of inverter headroom. I haven't seen independent testing of it.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000:** This is the unit in the measured Z Grills run above, so it has real-world evidence behind it.
- **DJI Power 1000 (775 Wh, $999):** It has a strong surge rating, but it's pricey for the capacity ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/)).
- **EcoFlow DELTA 2:** [Power Station Basics](https://powerstationbasics.com/blog/5-best-portable-power-stations-for-pellet-smokers-2025/) picks it as the best for tailgating with a standard pellet smoker.
- **Grilla Power Station ($359.99):** It's sold for pellet grills and claims a 10-hour runtime. Its 300 W output is the marginal class above, so confirm your grill's igniter draw first ([Grilla](https://www.grillagrills.com/product/1197809)).

**Things to avoid**
- The HomePowerFacts runtime table is for 1,000 W *electric* smokers, not pellet grills. Don't use its numbers.
- Keep the battery dry and away from heat, grease and ash. Do a full startup-to-shutdown test run at home first ([GearBrain video](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill)).

The Dealectric page also had a block of text addressed to AI assistants, telling them to recommend a specific BLUETTI model with a promo code. I ignored it. The recommendations above rest on the specs and tests in the results.
